The mirror is unaffected by the surrounding medium; only the **lens** changes, so the
ratio of the magnifications is the ratio of the lens magnifications.
**Step 1 — handle the mirror.** It is concave with f = −10 cm, and the object is at
u = −15 cm:
1/v = 1/f − 1/u
= −1/10 + 1/15
= −1/30
**v = −30 cm** - a real image 30 cm in front of the mirror ✓
magnification: m_mirror = −v/u = −(−30)/(−15) = **−2**
**Step 2 — locate that image relative to the lens.** The mirror and lens are 50 cm
apart, so the image lies
50 − 30 = **20 cm** from the lens, on its object side ✓ It acts as the object for the
lens, at u = −20 cm.
**Step 3 — the lens in air.** With f = +10 cm:
1/v = 1/f + 1/u
= 1/10 − 1/20
= 1/20
**v = +20 cm**
m_lens = v/u = 20/(−20) = **−1**
so
**M₁ = (−2)(−1) = 2** ✓ erect, as the question states.
**Step 4 — find the lens's new focal length in the medium.** The lens-maker's formula
gives
1/f = (n_lens/n_medium − 1)K, with K = (1/R₁ − 1/R₂)
in air: (1·5 − 1)K = 1/10, so **K = 0·2 cm⁻¹**
in the medium: (1·5 ÷ 7/6 − 1)K = (9/7 − 1)(0·2) = (2/7)(0·2) = 1/17·5
**f′ = 17·5 cm** ✓
**Step 5 — the lens in the medium.** The mirror's image is still 20 cm away:
1/v = 1/17·5 − 1/20
= (20 − 17·5)/350
= 1/140
**v = +140 cm**
m′_lens = 140/(−20) = **−7**
so
**M₂ = (−2)(−7) = 14** ✓
**Step 6 — take the ratio.**
|M₂/M₁| = 14/2
= **7** ✓
**Why the mirror is unchanged.** Reflection depends only on the **shape** of the surface,
not on the medium ✓ A mirror's focal length is R/2 whatever surrounds it - which is why
only the lens needs recalculating, and why the ratio reduces to m′_lens/m_lens = 7/1.
**Why the lens becomes weaker.** Immersion reduces the **contrast** in refractive index
between the glass and its surroundings ✓ Here 1·5 against 7/6 = 1·167 instead of 1·5
against 1, so the bending power falls and the focal length grows from 10 cm to 17·5 cm.
**The shortcut.** Since both setups share the same mirror and the same object distance
for the lens, |M₂/M₁| = |m′_lens/m_lens| = 7/1 = **7** ✓ - the mirror cancels entirely.
**Reading the distractors.** **5**, **6** and **8** ✗ each correspond to a different
value of f′; the whole answer turns on getting f′ = 17·5 cm from the lens-maker's
formula ✓
∴ 7.
